rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Resistance is resistivity times length over area. Metals have a positive temperature coefficient, so ρ and R rise when they are heated. Semiconductors usually do the opposite because more carriers are freed. The linear formula is only for a limited temperature range.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: α for many metals is about 0.004 per kelvin.  ·  The linear formula is a limited temperature range.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Resistance is R = ρ L / A. A longer wire has more resistance. A thicker wire has less. Resistivity ρ is the material property, independent of the particular length and area.  ·  The unit of resistivity is the ohm metre. A good conductor has a small resistivity. Glass and rubber have very large resistivities and are used as insulators.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Resistance depends on shape.  ·  Resistivity depends on the material.  ·  Metals increase in resistivity when heated.  ·  Semiconductors usually decrease.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Ohm's law: V = IR; R = ρL/A (resistivity ρ depends on material).  ·  Series: R = ΣR; same I, voltages add. Parallel: 1/R = Σ1/R; same V, currents add.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: For a metal over a moderate range, ρ = ρ_0 (1 + α ΔT), where α is the temperature coefficient. α is positive for metals, so heating raises the resistivity. More violent lattice vibrations scatter the electrons more often.  ·  The same linear form is used for resistance if the size does not change: R = R_0 (1 + α ΔT). A copper winding in a hot motor has a higher resistance than the cold value on the label.  ·  A semiconductor has a negative temperature coefficient. Heating frees more carriers, and the resistivity falls. That is why a thermistor can be used as a thermometer and why a semiconductor is not described by the metal formula with a positive α.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ ohm's law: v = ir; r = ρl/a (resistivity ρ depends on material)..  ·  Resistivity is not resistance.  ·  α for a metal is positive.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A semiconductor does not follow a positive α.  ·  L and A must be in metres and square metres if ρ is in ohm metres.  ·  Convert the area before using R = ρ L / A.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Say whether α is the metal value or a semiconductor.  ·  Write R = ρ L / A and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: ohm's law: v = ir; r = ρl/a (resistivity ρ depends on material).  ·  Alloys such as manganin are made so that α is nearly zero. They are used for standard resistors.
